title: Progress on stopping misuse of NRIC numbers in public and private sector transactions
asked: Mr Sharael Taha asked what progress has been made to ensure NRIC numbers are used appropriately across both public and private sector transactions.
response: Ms Jasmin Lau said the Government is working on two fronts: stopping the use of NRIC numbers as passwords for authentication, and moving away from partial NRIC numbers for identification. Government agencies stopped using NRIC numbers for authentication over a year ago, and the Personal Data Protection Commission and Cyber Security Agency have issued guidance to private organisations, with sector regulators working with telecommunications, finance and insurance, and healthcare. For identification, most agencies have stopped using NRIC numbers where accurate identification is not needed, and use the full NRIC number where it is, such as on licences and employment letters. The Government will consult the public before changing guidelines on partial NRIC numbers for the private sector, and has been running public education since June 2025.

key_points.point: Government agencies stopped using NRIC numbers for authentication over a year ago, and work is now under way with private organisations to do the same.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: Government agencies stopped this practice over a year ago and we are now working with private organisations to do the same.

key_points.point: The Personal Data Protection Commission and Cyber Security Agency have issued guidance to all private organisations.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: The Personal Data Protection Commission and Cyber Security Agency have issued guidance to all private organisations.

key_points.point: Organisations that flagrantly misuse NRIC numbers can be penalised under the Personal Data Protection Act.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: those that flagrantly misuse NRIC numbers can be penalised under the Personal Data Protection Act

key_points.point: Where there is no need to accurately identify someone, most agencies have stopped using the NRIC number completely.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: most agencies have stopped using the NRIC number completely

key_points.point: Where accurate identification is needed, agencies are starting to use the full NRIC number, such as on licences and employment letters issued by the Government.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: agencies are starting to use the full NRIC number instead, such as in official documents like licences and employment letters issued by the Government

key_points.point: For the private sector, the Government will consult the public before making any changes to guidelines on partial NRIC numbers.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: the Government will consult the public before making any changes to guidelines for the use of partial NRIC numbers

key_points.point: Public education on proper NRIC number use has been running since June 2025 through social media, traditional media, roadshows and community touchpoints.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: Since June 2025, we have been educating the public about proper NRIC number use through social media, traditional media, roadshows and community touchpoints.

key_points.point: The national campaign will continue across multiple platforms in English and vernacular languages.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: We will continue our national campaign across multiple platforms in English and vernacular languages

key_points.point: The public is encouraged to keep reporting cases where NRIC numbers are mishandled during the transition period.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: we encourage the public to continue reporting cases where NRIC numbers are mishandled

left_open: A specific date by which private-sector organisations must stop using NRIC numbers for authentication.
The timeline for any changes to private-sector guidelines on partial NRIC numbers, which will follow public consultation.
